title: Utility Order for Washington - St. Tammany Electric Cooperative, Inc., ex parte. — Order No. U-37927 accepts the Joint Report for the 2025 Test Year Formula Rate Plan filing submitted on August 24, 2026, which found that no rate change was necessary and was in accordance with the terms of Washington-St. Tammany Electric Cooperative (“WST”) Formula Rate Plan. The Order also allowed WST to create a regulatory liability to flow back to ratepayers, subject to the conditions within. This matter was considered at the September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                   ORDER NUMBER U-37927

   WASHINGTON - ST. TAMMANY ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE, INC., EX PARTE.

Docket No. U-37927, In re: Formula Rate Plan annual earnings monitoring report for test year
ending on December 31, 2025.

              (Decided at the September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                             ORDER

Overview and Procedural History

       The Louisiana Public Service Commission (“Commission”), having reviewed and

considered the Joint Report and Draft Order on Washington-St. Tammany Electric Cooperative,

Inc.’s Formula Rate Plan Annual Report Filing for the Test Year Ending December 31, 2025

(“Joint Report”) submitted by the Louisiana Public Service Commission Staff (“Staff”) and

Washington-St. Tammany Electric Cooperative, Inc. (“WST” or “Cooperative”), finds the Joint

Report, together with its attached exhibits, to be acceptable and in accordance with the provisions

of the Commission’s Order No. U-36399 dated May 5, 2023, which established the Cooperative’s

current Formula Rate Plan (“FRP”) for test years 2022-2025. The Joint Report was filed into the

record on August 24, 2026.



       The Joint Report indicated that, after adjustments, WST earned a Times Interest Earned

Ratio (“TIER”) that fell within the bandwidth prescribed in the Cooperative’s FRP and, therefore,

that no change in rates is required.




Commission Jurisdiction and Authority


       The Commission exercises jurisdiction over public utilities in Louisiana pursuant to Article

4, Section 21(B) of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana, which provides the following:

               The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
               utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law.
               It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and
               procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have
               other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.




                                                                               Order No. U-37927
                                                                                          Page 1
        Pursuant to its constitutional authority, the Commission issued Order No. U-36399, which

established WST’s current FRP. The Cooperative’s FRP provides for a TIER bandwidth with a

lower endpoint of 1.40, an upper endpoint of 1.60, and a midpoint of 1.50, as well as a lower limit

Modified Debt Service Coverage Ratio (“MDSC”) of 1.40 and a lower limit Operating Times

Interest Earned Ratio (“OTIER”) of 1.20. Under the FRP, if a test year’s TIER is less than 1.40 or

greater than 1.60, WST’s FRP Rider revenue is to be increased or decreased, respectively, by the

amount necessary to increase or decrease the TIER to reach the midpoint of 1.50. Additionally, if

a test year’s MDSC is less than the lower limit of 1.40 or OTIER is less than the lower limit of

1.20, WST’s FRP Rider revenue is to be increased by the amount necessary to increase the MDSC

or OTIER to reach the respective lower limit.




Commission Consideration


       The Commission considered this matter at its September 16, 2026 Business and Executive

Session. After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Francis,

and unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to accept the Joint Report and issue the Draft

Order filed into the record on August 24, 2026.




THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED THAT:

   1. The Commission accepts the Joint Report filed on August 24, 2026, and issues the Draft

       Order attached thereto.

   2. WST is authorized to create a regulatory liability of approximately $2.6 million to flow

       back to its ratepayers on a kilowatt-hour (kWh) basis over a period of twelve (12) months

       at approximately $0.00254 per kWh.

   3. The Commission agrees with WST’s methodology regarding Generation and Transmission

       Credits for the 2025 test year but reserves the right to change its opinion on this issue in

       future proceedings.

   4. In its next rate case filing, WST shall address the inclusion of Generation and Transmission

       Credits or any other non-cash patronage capital that is allocated to it in regard to rate-setting

       methodologies in any future rate structure.



                                                                                  Order No. U-37927
                                                                                             Page 2
    5. Within thirty (30) days after the issuance of this Order, WST shall submit an updated and

       revised tariff reflecting the Commission’s action to the Commission’s Utilities Division

       and Legal Division for their review and approval. WST shall not implement the rates

       authorized by this Order unless and until Commission Staff receives and approves the

       Cooperative’s updated and revised tariff.

This order is effective immediately.

BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
October 12, 2026
